note: Buhari's first full budget, the 'Budget of Change', was delayed for months and only signed in May 2016. Actual oil revenue collapsed well below projection amid the price crash and Niger Delta Avengers pipeline attacks, tipping Nigeria into its first recession in 25 years by Q2 2016. Capital release was among the lowest of the era.

note: The 'Budget of Recovery and Growth' accompanied Nigeria's exit from recession in Q2 2017, launched alongside the Economic Recovery and Growth Plan (ERGP). Capital implementation improved from the prior year but still fell well short of the ambitious ERGP infrastructure targets.

The 'Budget of Consolidation' was not signed until June 2018 — over five months into the fiscal year — after a prolonged dispute between the executive and National Assembly over budget padding. The late signing compressed the effective implementation window for capital projects.

note: The 'Budget of Continuity' was presented in an election year; recurrent spending (including election-related security costs) grew faster than capital allocation, which fell as a share of the total compared with 2018.

Originally signed in December 2019 as a ₦10.33 trillion budget benchmarked at $57/barrel — the earliest budget signing in years — the 2020 budget was drastically revised mid-year after the COVID-19 oil price crash, cutting the benchmark to $28/barrel and slashing revenue projections. Actual revenue still undershot even the revised target as the economy contracted.
